info.name: Conductor API
info.description:
Conductor API collection, organized in folders by resource. It covers authentication, tenants, users, credentials, model runner endpoints (all nine endpoint types, including Anthropic, TypeSafe, Ollaya, OllamaCloud and OpenAICompatible), endpoint groups, model definitions, model configurations, load-balancing policies, QoS, model access policies, virtual model runners, VMR reservations, model loading, request history, analytics, validation and preview, routing explanation, endpoint states, observability, administrators, backup and restore, and the proxied Anthropic and TypeSafe decision APIs.

Setup: set `baseUrl` (default http://127.0.0.1:9000) and `bearerToken` (a Conductor credential bearer token; use the Authentication folder to obtain one). Every request inherits collection-level Bearer auth from `{{bearerToken}}` unless it says otherwise. The Tenants and Administrators folders instead send the system administrator API key from `{{adminApiKey}}` in the `x-admin-apikey` header, because those routes require a system administrator. `tenantId` (default `default`, the tenant created on first run) is sent as `TenantId` in create, validate and update bodies and as `?tenantId=` on routes that take it. Global-admin credentials, including the first-run token, use it to pick a tenant; a write without it acts on the credential's own tenant. System administrator credentials have no tenant, so their writes must include it (400 otherwise). Other credentials always act in their own tenant and the value is ignored. Proxied requests need a credential in the VMR's own tenant, including for global admins; a credential from another tenant gets 403 CredentialTenantMismatch. Create requests store the new resource ID in a collection variable through a test script, so later requests in the same folder can use it.

Upstream provider keys (`anthropicUpstreamApiKey`, `typesafeUpstreamApiKey`, `ollamaCloudUpstreamApiKey`) are empty by default; set them in your environment, never in the collection. Responses always mask endpoint API keys as **** plus the last four characters; use Reveal Endpoint API Key to read the full value. See REST_API.md for every route's parameters, bodies and status codes.

item.name: Authentication

request.description: Log in with tenant ID, email and password. Public. Returns 200 with a bearer token, or 401 for bad credentials.
Exchange an existing credential bearer token for session details. Public. Returns 200, or 401.
Log in as a system administrator with email and password. Public. Returns 200, or 401.

item.description: Obtain a bearer token. Login routes are public. Copy the returned token into the `bearerToken` variable.

item.name: Tenants

request.description: List tenants. Requires authentication: system administrators and global admin users see every tenant; other users see only their own tenant, and the paging and filter parameters do not apply to them. Optional query parameters: maxResults, continuationToken, nameFilter, activeFilter. Returns 200 with Data, TotalCount and HasMore, or 401 without credentials.
Read one tenant by ID. Requires a global admin user or a system administrator. Returns 200, 401 for other callers, or 404 when the tenant does not exist.

Create a tenant. Requires a system administrator (this folder sends x-admin-apikey). Returns 201 with the stored tenant, 400 when validation fails, or 401 for any other caller, including global admin users.
Update a tenant. Requires a system administrator. Returns 200 with the stored tenant, 400 when validation fails, 401 for any other caller, or 404.

Delete a tenant and all of its data. Requires a system administrator. Request history (entries, analytics events and detail files) is deleted first, then the tenant's other resources. Returns 204, 401 for any other caller, or 404 when it does not exist.

System-administrator only (other callers get 401), destructive nuke. Permanently and irreversibly deletes the tenant and ALL of its associated data (users, credentials, virtual model runners, endpoints, load-balancing and model-access policies, reservations, QoS profiles, request history, and analytics). The request body must include ConfirmTenantId, and its value MUST exactly match the tenant id in the URL path; if they do not match the request is rejected without deleting anything. The default tenant cannot be purged: the endpoint refuses the request. This action cannot be undone.

item.description: Tenant management. Every tenant route requires authentication. Create, update, delete and purge require a system administrator; reading one tenant requires a global admin user or a system administrator; listing works for any authenticated caller, but users who are not global admins see only their own tenant. Requests in this folder authenticate as a system administrator with the x-admin-apikey header from `{{adminApiKey}}` (folder-level API key auth). To try List Tenants or Get Tenant as a global admin user instead, switch the request's auth to Inherit or Bearer with `{{bearerToken}}`. Calls without credentials, or below the required level, return 401.

item.name: Users

request.description: List users visible to the caller. Optional query parameters: maxResults, continuationToken, nameFilter, activeFilter, tenantId. Returns 200 with Data, ContinuationToken, TotalCount and HasMore. Responses never contain Password.
Read one user by ID. Returns 200, or 404 when it does not exist in the caller's tenant. The response never contains Password.
Create a user. Cross-tenant callers supply TenantId in the body. Returns 201 with the stored user, or 400 when validation fails. The response never contains Password.

Update a user. An omitted Password keeps the stored one, so a user read from the API can be sent back unchanged. Returns 200 with the stored user (without Password), 400 when validation fails, or 404.
Delete a user. Returns 204, or 404 when it does not exist.

item.description: User CRUD within a tenant. Requires a tenant admin or global admin.

item.name: Credentials

request.description: List credentials visible to the caller. Optional query parameters: maxResults, continuationToken, nameFilter, activeFilter, tenantId. Returns 200 with Data, ContinuationToken, TotalCount and HasMore.
Read one credential by ID. Returns 200, or 404 when it does not exist in the caller's tenant.

Create a credential. Cross-tenant callers supply TenantId in the body. UserId names the owner and must be a user in the target tenant (400 otherwise); without UserId the credential belongs to the caller. A system administrator has no user, so it must supply UserId. Returns 201 with the stored credential, including its BearerToken.

Replace a credential's Name, Active, Labels, Tags and Metadata. UserId and CreatedUtc are kept from the stored record. Omit BearerToken (or send an empty string) to keep the existing token; a new BearerToken must be unique. Cross-tenant callers supply TenantId in the body.
Delete a credential. Returns 204, or 404 when it does not exist.

item.description: Credential (bearer token) CRUD within a tenant. Requires a tenant admin or global admin. A credential is what clients send to Conductor, including as x-api-key on Anthropic VMRs.

item.name: Model Runner Endpoints

request.description: List model runner endpoints visible to the caller. Optional query parameters: maxResults, continuationToken, nameFilter, activeFilter, tenantId. Returns 200 with Data, ContinuationToken, TotalCount and HasMore. ApiKey is masked in the response.
Read one model runner endpoint by ID. Returns 200, or 404 when it does not exist in the caller's tenant. ApiKey is masked in the response.

body.raw:
{
  "TenantId": "{{tenantId}}",
  "Name": "My Ollama Server",
  "ApiType": "Ollama",
  "Hostname": "127.0.0.1",
  "Port": 11434,
  "UseSsl": false,
  "HealthCheckUrl": "/",
  "HealthCheckMethod": "GET",
  "HealthCheckExpectedStatusCode": 200,
  "RigMonitor": {
    "Enabled": true,
    "Port": 9990,
    "UseSsl": false,
    "CollectDuringHealthCheck": true,
    "RequireReadyz": true,
    "HealthAffectedByRigMonitor": false,
    "TelemetryProfile": "GpuPlacement"
  }
}

request.description: Create a model runner endpoint. Cross-tenant callers supply TenantId in the body. Returns 201 with the stored resource, or 400 when validation fails. ApiKey is masked in the response. Omitted host, port, SSL and health check fields are filled from the ApiType defaults.

body.raw:
{
  "TenantId": "{{tenantId}}",
  "Name": "Updated Endpoint",
  "RigMonitor": {
    "Enabled": true,
    "HostnameOverride": "rigmonitor-host.local",
    "Port": 9990,
    "UseSsl": false,
    "TimeoutMs": 5000,
    "CollectDuringHealthCheck": true,
    "RequireReadyz": true,
    "HealthAffectedByRigMonitor": false,
    "MaxTelemetryAgeMs": 30000,
    "CapabilitiesRefreshIntervalMs": 60000,
    "TelemetryProfile": "Custom",
    "TelemetrySelectors": ["system", "cpu", "memory", "gpu"]
  }
}

request.description: Update a model runner endpoint. Returns 200 with the stored resource, 400 when validation fails, or 404. ApiKey is masked in the response. An omitted, null or masked ApiKey keeps the stored key; an empty string clears it.
Delete a model runner endpoint. Returns 204, or 404 when it does not exist.
Cached health state for every endpoint in scope. Endpoints with HealthCheckEnabled=false report healthy without being probed. Returns 200.
Cached health state for one endpoint: IsHealthy, uptime, consecutive results, in-flight count, service state and history. Returns 200, or 404.
Tenant admin. Lists local models on an Ollama endpoint through GET /api/tags. Returns 400 for OllamaCloud and other types.
Tenant admin. Pulls a model onto an Ollama endpoint (POST /api/pull, stream=false). Returns 400 for OllamaCloud and other types.
Tenant admin. Deletes a local model from an Ollama endpoint. Returns 400 for OllamaCloud and other types.
Cached RigMonitor readiness, capabilities and telemetry for one endpoint. RigMonitor is not supported for OllamaCloud endpoints.

Create an Anthropic endpoint. Only Name, ApiType and ApiKey are sent; the server applies the Anthropic type defaults: api.anthropic.com, port 443, SSL, health check GET /v1/models?limit=1 with auth, enabled, every 60000 ms. The key is sent upstream in x-api-key with anthropic-version. AnthropicVersion is optional (yyyy-MM-dd; null uses Settings.Anthropic.DefaultVersion). Returns 201 with ApiKey masked, or 400 with AnthropicApiKeyMissing when no key is set. Stores the ID in anthropicEndpointId.

exec: pm.test('ApiKey is masked or null', function () {

request.description: Create a hosted TypeSafe endpoint for Jev decision models. Type defaults: api.typesafe.ai, port 443, SSL, health check POST /v1/systemone with a one-question decision probe body. Hosted TypeSafe has no /v1/models route and each probe is billed, so HealthCheckEnabled defaults to false (the endpoint is treated as healthy). Set HealthCheckEnabled to true to probe every 60000 ms. Returns 201, or 400 with TypeSafeApiKeyMissing. Stores the ID in typesafeEndpointId.

exec: pm.test('ApiKey is masked or null', function () {

request.description: Create a local Ollaya endpoint (System One decision API). Endpoint-only: attach it to a TypeSafe VMR. Type defaults: 127.0.0.1, no SSL, health check GET /v1/models without auth every 5000 ms. The key is optional. Port is required: Ollaya has no default port, so a create without it fails with PortRequired. An update that omits Port keeps the stored port. Returns 201. Stores the ID in ollayaEndpointId.

Create an Ollama Cloud endpoint. Endpoint-only: attach it to an Ollama VMR. Type defaults: ollama.com, port 443, SSL, health check GET /api/tags with auth every 60000 ms. A key is required (OllamaCloudApiKeyMissing). Model management, keep-warm and RigMonitor are not supported. Returns 201.

exec: pm.test('ApiKey is masked or null', function () {

request.description: Create an OpenAI-compatible endpoint (LM Studio, llama.cpp, Ollama /v1, and similar). Endpoint-only: attach it to an OpenAI VMR. Type defaults: 127.0.0.1, no SSL, health check GET /v1/models without auth every 5000 ms. The key is optional. Model load reports Verified. Port is required: OpenAICompatible has no default port, so a create without it fails with PortRequired. An update that omits Port keeps the stored port. Returns 201.

Return the full, unmasked upstream API key of an endpoint: {"ApiKey":"..."}. When no key is set the body is {}. Requires a tenant admin, a global admin user, or a system administrator; standard users get 401 even though they can read and update endpoints. Tenant admins can reveal keys only in their own tenant; cross-tenant callers add ?tenantId=. Every call writes an audit log line that does not contain the key. Returns 200, 401, or 404.

exec: pm.test('Body holds the unmasked key or nothing', function () {

item.description: Upstream model runner endpoints. ApiType is one of Ollama, OpenAI, Gemini, vLLM, Anthropic, TypeSafe, Ollaya, OllamaCloud, OpenAICompatible. The server fills type defaults (host, port, SSL, health check) for fields a create request omits; nothing is inferred from the hostname. ApiKey is masked in every response; an omitted, null or masked ApiKey on update keeps the stored key, and "" clears it. Auth: any authenticated user in the tenant; Ollama model management requires a tenant admin.

item.description: Reusable parameter sets and pinned properties applied to completion and embedding requests. Never applied to decision requests.

item.name: Load Balancing Policies

request.description: List load-balancing policys visible to the caller. Optional query parameters: maxResults, continuationToken, nameFilter, activeFilter, tenantId. Returns 200 with Data, ContinuationToken, TotalCount and HasMore.
Read one load-balancing policy by ID. Returns 200, or 404 when it does not exist in the caller's tenant.
Create a load-balancing policy. Cross-tenant callers supply TenantId in the body. Returns 201 with the stored resource, or 400 when validation fails.

Lists the metric names that load-balancing policy filters and rankings can use. Returns 200.

item.description: First-class policies that filter and rank endpoints using health, capacity and RigMonitor metrics.

item.name: QoS Profiles
item.description: Manage Quality-of-Service (QoS) profiles: named queueing topologies of nodes, disciplines, traffic classes, rules, links, and ingress routes that shape how requests are admitted, prioritized, and drained. Endpoints support listing with pagination and filtering, create, validate-before-save, class-selector catalog lookup, read, update, and delete. All requests inherit the collection-level bearer auth; supply the tenant scope via the tenantId variable where applicable.

query.description: Maximum number of profiles to return in one page. Optional.
Opaque token from a previous page used to fetch the next page of results. Optional.
Case-insensitive substring filter applied to the profile name. Optional.
Filter by active state: 'true' returns only active profiles, 'false' only inactive. Optional; omit to return all.
Scope the listing to a specific tenant. Optional; system administrators may enumerate across tenants.

request.description: List QoS profiles with optional pagination and filtering. Enable the query parameters as needed to page through results or narrow by name, active state, or tenant.

Create a QoS profile. The example body defines a minimal single-node FIFO topology: one node named 'root' using the Fifo discipline, unbounded depth (MaxDepth 0), a Reject overflow policy, no per-node classes, and empty Rules, Links, and IngressRoutes. IngressMode 'Single' with IngressDefaultNode and TailNode both pointing at the single node.

Validate a QoS profile definition without saving it. Returns validation results describing any structural or referential errors (unknown node references, missing default class, invalid disciplines, dangling links or ingress routes) so the topology can be corrected before create or update. Uses the same body shape as Create.

Return the catalog of classifier fields and operators available for building QoS rules and class selectors. Use this to discover which request attributes can be matched and how, when authoring profile rules.
Read a single QoS profile by its identifier. Set the qosProfileId collection variable to the profile id.

Update an existing QoS profile by its identifier, replacing its topology definition. Set the qosProfileId collection variable to the profile id. The example body mirrors Create with an adjusted MaxQueueWaitMs.
Delete a QoS profile by its identifier. Set the qosProfileId collection variable to the profile id.

item.name: QoS Traffic Classes
item.description: Manage QoS traffic classes: named service tiers (for example Interactive, Batch, or Bulk) that requests are mapped to and that QoS profiles reference when prioritizing and shaping traffic. Endpoints support listing, create, read, update, and delete. All requests inherit the collection-level bearer auth.

request.description: List all QoS traffic classes.

Create a QoS traffic class. Provide a Name, an optional human-readable Description, and a Tier (for example 'Interactive', 'Batch', or 'Bulk') that determines how the class is prioritized by QoS profiles.
Read a single QoS traffic class by its identifier. Set the qosTrafficClassId collection variable to the class id.
Update an existing QoS traffic class by its identifier. Set the qosTrafficClassId collection variable to the class id.
Delete a QoS traffic class by its identifier. Set the qosTrafficClassId collection variable to the class id.

item.name: QoS Runtime
item.description: Read-only live QoS runtime state: per-VMR scheduler state, admission capacity usage, queue depth, per-class admission statistics, endpoint concurrency, and time-bucketed admission history. Runtime state is held in server memory and resets when the server restarts. Global administrators may pass tenantId to scope the request. All requests inherit the collection-level bearer auth.

query.description: Tenant to read (global administrators only). Omit for tenant-scoped credentials.

request.description: List the QoS runtime snapshot of every virtual model runner in scope, ordered by runner name. Each snapshot includes SchedulerState (Running, Recovering, PassThrough, or Idle), Capacity, InUse, Waiting, MaxQueueWaitMs, per-class Classes statistics, and Endpoints concurrency.

query.description: Tenant to read (global administrators only). Omit for tenant-scoped credentials.

request.description: Read the QoS runtime snapshot of a single virtual model runner. Set the vmrId collection variable to the runner id. Returns 404 when the runner does not exist in scope.

query.description: Window start (ISO-8601 UTC). Defaults to one hour before endUtc.
Window end (ISO-8601 UTC). Defaults to now.
Bucket interval: minute (default), 5minute, 15minute, or hour.
Tenant to read (global administrators only). Omit for tenant-scoped credentials.

request.description: Read time-bucketed QoS admission history for a virtual model runner: per-class Admitted, Rejected, TimedOut, Aborted, and EndpointSlotTimeouts counts, AverageWaitMs, MaxWaitMs, and PeakWaiting per bucket. Buckets without activity are omitted. The window may not exceed 24 hours; an invalid timestamp, interval, or window returns 400. Set the vmrId collection variable to the runner id.

request.description: Validate a policy draft and its nested rules without saving it. Returns 200 with a ResourceValidationResult.

item.name: Proxied APIs
item.description: Requests sent through virtual model runners rather than the management API. Each subfolder targets a VMR created in the Virtual Model Runners folder. Requests are classified by the VMR's configured ApiType: a path outside the type's namespace returns 404 without being forwarded. Paths with dot segments or encoded separators return 404 (UnsafePath). Authentication uses the collection bearer token (a Conductor credential), which must belong to the VMR's tenant: a credential from another tenant, including a global admin's, gets 403 CredentialTenantMismatch. Conductor-generated errors carry their reason code in the X-Conductor-Error-Code header. Upstream provider keys stay on the endpoints.

item.name: Anthropic
item.description: Anthropic Messages API through the Anthropic VMR at {{anthropicVmrBasePath}}. Inbound credentials: Authorization Bearer or x-api-key (Anthropic VMRs only). anthropic-version: client header, then the endpoint AnthropicVersion, then Settings.Anthropic.DefaultVersion. Conductor-generated errors use the Anthropic error shape {"type":"error","error":{"type","message"}} with X-Conductor-Error-Code; upstream errors pass through unchanged.

request.description: Anthropic create message (AnthropicMessages, model access action Completions). Authenticated with the collection bearer token, a Conductor credential. Conductor sends the endpoint key upstream in x-api-key and the client anthropic-version. Response headers request-id, retry-after, x-should-retry and anthropic-ratelimit-* are copied back. Usage, including cache token counts, is recorded in request history.
Streaming create message. The server-sent event stream is passed through unchanged. Input tokens are taken from message_start and output tokens from the last message_delta.
Anthropic count tokens (AnthropicCountTokens, action Completions). Classified as a metadata request by the Inference First QoS profile for newly seeded tenants.
Anthropic list models (AnthropicListModels, action ListModels). With ModelAccessControl.ListModelsBehavior Filter or Synthesize the list keeps the Anthropic shape: data, has_more, first_id, last_id.
Anthropic get model (AnthropicGetModel, action ShowModel).

Negative example: Message Batches and Files are stateful and not supported through Conductor. Returns 404 in the Anthropic error shape with not_found_error and X-Conductor-Error-Code UnsupportedRoute. Nothing is forwarded upstream.

Authenticates with the Conductor credential in x-api-key instead of Authorization, the way Anthropic clients send their key. Accepted on Anthropic VMRs only; other VMR types return 401. The header is never forwarded upstream. A bad credential returns 401 with authentication_error.

item.name: Decision
item.description: TypeSafe System One decision API through the TypeSafe VMR at {{typesafeVmrBasePath}}. A request has model, state and questions; question types are noul (binary), choice and score. Bodies with no questions, more than TypeSafe.MaxQuestionsPerRequest (default 64) questions, or invalid JSON get 400. Responses are not streamed. Request history records the DecisionQuestionCount.

request.description: TypeSafe System One decision with one binary (noul) question. Classified as TypeSafeDecide and governed by the Decisions model access action. The answer is a probability, for example {"noul":0.97}. Model configurations are never applied.
Decision with one choice question. criteria maps each option to a description or null. The answer names the chosen option with per-option probabilities.
Decision with one score question. criteria is an ordered list of levels and the answer is a score on that scale.

Negative example: the pre-request script builds 65 questions, one more than the default TypeSafe.MaxQuestionsPerRequest. Conductor returns 400 with Code DecisionRequestInvalid before routing, and nothing is forwarded. Empty questions and invalid JSON are rejected the same way.

exec: // Build a decision body with one more question than the default TypeSafe.MaxQuestionsPerRequest (64).
for (let i = 0; i < 65; i++) { questions['q' + i] = { type: 'noul', instructions: 'Is item ' + i + ' relevant?' }; }
pm.variables.set('decisionTooManyBody', JSON.stringify({ model: pm.variables.get('decisionModel'), state: 'test', questions: questions }));

request.description: TypeSafe list models (TypeSafeListModels, action ListModels). Ollaya serves this route; hosted TypeSafe does not, so with only a hosted endpoint the upstream status passes through. With ListModelsBehavior Synthesize the list is built from the VMR model definitions in the {"object":"list","data":[...]} shape.

exec: pm.test('Status is 200 or an upstream pass-through', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.code).to.be.below(500); });
if (pm.response.code === 200) { pm.test('data is an array', function () { pm.expect(pm.response.json().data).to.be.an('array'); }); }
